data.title: Anthropic weighs launching a new AI model ahead of IPO: Reuters
data.description:
Anthropic (ANTHRO) is planning to release a new AI model ahead of its much-anticipated IPO in a bid to rival OpenAI’s (OPENAI) newfound momentum in enterprise AI following the recent launch of the ChatGPT maker’s GPT-6 Astra model, Reuters reported, citing three sources familiar with the matter.

The report comes days after Anthropic (ANTHRO) CEO Dario Amodei, along with other tech CEOs, including OpenAI’s (OPENAI) Sam Altman, called for a slowdown in the pace of AI development.

In a 3,800-word essay posted last Saturday, Amodei said, "We must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models,” a view that drew support from Altman and SpaceX (SPCX) CEO Elon Musk.

The company is assessing the safety of ​its next model alongside plans for the launch, according to one of the people familiar with the matter.

Another point being discussed is how to strike a balance between new model rollouts and improving the company’s profitability as investors become more focused on the timing of anticipated profits amid rising interest rates, people familiar with the company’s thinking said.

Anthropic (ANTHRO) didn’t respond to Reuters’ requests for comment.

According to the latest data from corporate expense platform Ramp, GPT-6 Astra, released earlier this month, has already accounted for about 13% of enterprise AI spending compared with about 8% for Anthropic’s (ANTHRO) Claude Fable.

Meta Platforms (META) has been among the top customers of Anthropic (ANTHRO). However, the social media company is looking to cut its reliance on Anthropic’s models as it focuses more on developing AI capabilities internally, people familiar with the matter said.

Anthropic (ANTHRO) weighs launching its blockbuster IPO in November, a delayed timeline compared to its prior expectations as the AI industry confronts growing calls for a slowdown in the pace of model development, The Wall Street Journal reported Friday.

data.title: Warner Bros. jumps on report of settlement talks with California AG
data.description:
Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) soared 8.3% in after-hours trading after a report that Paramount Skydance (PSKY) is in advanced settlement talks with California officials over a lawsuit to block the $110 billion mega media deal, according to a  WSJ report on Friday, which cited people familiar with the matter. 

A settlement could come as soon as this weekend, according to a separate  Reuters report late Friday, which cited people familiar with the matter. Independent monitoring of CNN is one of the terms in the settlement talks, as well as a commitment to the number of theatrical releases.

A spokesperson for the California Department of ​Justice said potential ​settlement talks ⁠are confidential. "We cannot confirm or deny whether settlement talks are occurring or their ​alleged substance," the spokesperson told Reuters. Paramount declined to ​comment.

A dozen state AGs, led by California, sued to block the mega media deal in July. A trial is scheduled for March on the combination. On Tuesday, a court ordered Paramount (PSKY) and California AG Rob Bonta to meet Oct. 14 to try to work on a potential settlement.

Shares of Paramount (PSKY) jumped 7.6% in after-hours trading. 

Under the terms of the merger agreement, Paramount (PSKY) must pay Warner Bros. (WBD) shareholders $650M per quarter beginning October 1. Because the trial is set for March 2027, Paramount would be required to pay $1.3B in ticking fees plus another $190M in incremental financing costs and legal fees.

data.title: Oil falls for third straight day as Saudi supply disruptions look less severe than feared
data.description:
Crude oil futures extended declines to a third consecutive session Friday, as market watchers believed the closure of Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline may have a less severe impact on supply than originally feared.

While concerns remain about the Middle East war dragging on and shipping restrictions through the Strait of Hormuz, reports that the pipeline could resume partial flows within days helped oil futures pull back from four-month highs reached earlier this week.

However, repairing damaged pumping stations and fully restoring capacity could take as long as 6-8 weeks, analysts have said.

A ship-to-ship shuttle service through the strait under U.S. military protection, with oil transferred to other tankers waiting in the Gulf of Oman, reportedly could provide Saudi Arabia with another option for getting crude to buyers.

"Middle East oil flows remain surprisingly strong despite the disruption to Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline," J.P. Morgan head of global commodities strategy Natasha Kaneva said in a note, estimating total oil flows from the Middle East averaged ~17M bbl/day over the past 10 days, nearly 75% of the 2025 average.

Satellite imagery suggests the Saudis have moved 2.8M bbl/day through Hormuz over the past six days compared to just 700K bbl/day in August, the analyst said, while cautioning that the volumes could be difficult to sustain.

Meanwhile, physical premiums for oil in the North Sea, a key reference for global prices, soared to record levels Friday, after Saudi Aramco (ARMCO) told European customers they would not receive any supplies under their long-term agreements next month.

Norway's Johan Sverdrup, a grade of crude closely comparable with Saudi supplies, was offered at a premium of as much as $35/bbl above the Dated Brent physical benchmark, Bloomberg reported, after the same oil traded at a $0.60 premium less than two weeks earlier.

In the U.S., average retail prices for regular gasoline rose to $4.47/gal on Friday from $4.30 a week ago, AAA reported, while average diesel prices hit another new all-time high of $6.45/gal.

Front-month Nymex crude (CL1:COM) for October delivery slipped 1.6% to $100.30/bbl, front-month Brent crude (CO1:COM) for November delivery dropped 0.9% to $103.87/bbl, while front-month Nymex October natural gas (NG1:COM) rose 0.4% to $2.912/MMBtu.

For the week, Nymex crude and Brent crude rose 0.2% and 0.7%, respectively, and Nymex natural gas gained 2.8%.

Energy stocks, as represented by the State Street Energy Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLE), declined 1.3% this week.

data.title: NASA in talks for Boeing's Starliner for 10 or more new missions - WSJ
data.description:
Boeing (BA) and NASA are in talks about using the company's Starliner vehicle to handle 10 or more new flights to low-Earth orbit in the coming years, The Wall Street Journal reported Friday.

The Starliner has not flown since summer 2024, when performance problems including failed thrusters that posed safety risks left two astronauts stuck on the International Space Station for months; the astronauts returned to Earth on SpaceX's Crew Dragon vehicle, eschewing the Starliner, which came back empty.

The Crew Dragon has been the only certified vehicle to carry NASA astronauts to the space station from the U.S., but SpaceX has stopped making new Dragon ships; the company has not said publicly when it plans to stop operating the ship.

NASA said Friday it awarded SpaceX three additional astronaut missions to the space station using Crew Dragon; the flights are worth an average of $315M each and run through 2030.

There are few other options for flights to low-Earth orbit; Northrop Grumman has a cargo capsule that flies to the space station for NASA, but not a human-rated one, while Russia flies vehicles to the ISS that handle crews and cargo.

data.title: InMed receives Nasdaq notice over equity requirement
S&P 500 ends volatile week as Fed hikes rates, yields jump, oil surges
data.description:
The benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) inched up 0.1% at 7,650.50 points on Friday to close the volatile week that saw the Federal Reserve deliver its first interest rate hike in three years, Treasury yields climb above 5%, and oil prices remain above $100 a barrel.

The index was down 0.1% for the week.

The Fed raised its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points on Wednesday to a range of 3.75%-4%. The 10-year Treasury yield briefly topped 5% during the week, reaching its highest level since 2007. Crude prices also surged this week after damage to Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline raised concerns about supply disruptions. Prices retreated from highs of $106 as fears of a prolonged disruption eased, but crude remained above $100 a barrel on Friday.

This week's Friday also coincided with quadruple witching, which is when stock-index futures, stock-index options, stock options, and single-stock futures expire, which contributes to volatility.

Technology leads sector gains

Technology was the S&P 500's strongest-performing sector for the week, with the Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLK) gaining 3.69%. The advance was driven largely by a rebound in semiconductor and chip-equipment stocks. On Friday, Broadcom (AVGO), up 3%, and Lam Research (LRCX) and Applied Materials (AMAT), up about 7%, were among the notable gainers.

The technology sector had started the week under pressure after an AI-related selloff, but chip stocks recovered later in the week. 

Other S&P 500 sectors were mostly lower. Communication Services (XLC) fell 2.5%, Financials (XLF) dropped 2.63%, Utilities (XLU) lost 2.95%, Consumer Staples (XLP) declined 1.77%, Consumer Discretionary (XLY) slipped 1.17%, Materials (XLB) fell 1.40%, Real Estate (XLRE) dropped 2%, and Energy (XLE) declined 2.44%.

Industrials (XLI) gained 0.62%, and Health Care (XLV) rose 0.30%.

data.title: Gold ekes out weekly gain despite Fed rate hike
data.description:
Gold futures edged higher Friday and for the week, showing surprising resilience even after the U.S. Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time since 2023 and signaled further tightening by year-end.

Analysts have said investors are increasingly looking beyond incremental changes in interest rates and focusing on the much larger structural forces supporting gold, including deteriorating government finances, persistent inflation, geopolitical uncertainty, and changing global reserve allocations.

Gold and silver are "once again holding key support levels—a positive sign that the metals rally may be poised to gain traction despite the higher cost of money," Spartan Capital's Peter Cardillo said in a note.

"Gold's resilience is notable given that the Fed has just begun a new hiking cycle and the dollar remains relatively firm, suggesting continued demand from investors less sensitive to the traditional rates-and-dollar relationship," Saxo Bank Head of Commodity Strategy Ole Hansen wrote, noting that holdings in gold-backed ETFs have climbed to a seven-month high despite the metal's recent price weakness.

The yellow metal also climbed as the pullback in oil prices eased concerns around inflation and future rate hikes from the Fed, analysts at ANZ Research said.

Front-month Comex gold (XAUUSD:CUR) for September delivery gained 0.6% to $4,385.90/oz, and front-month Comex September silver (XAGUSD:CUR) delivery climbed 1.6% to $66.556/oz; for the full week, gold and silver rose 0.4% and 3.1%, respectively.

data.title: OpenAI's Altman plans to address UN Security Council due to mounting concerns: report
data.description:
OpenAI (OPENAI) CEO Sam Altman plans to address the United Nations Security Council next week in New York City during the U.N. General Assembly, according to Reuters.

The U.N. Security Council is slated to meet on Wednesday, Sept. 23.

"Sam Altman will brief an open UN Security Council meeting in person ​next week," said an OpenAI spokesperson, according to the report. "His remarks are ​expected to focus on the steps OpenAI is taking to ensure AI ‌is ⁠safe and benefits people globally, along with the need for international coordination and shared safety standards."

The meeting takes place in the wake of AI company executives calling for a deliberate pacing of AI model development due to its ever-increasing capabilities, particularly in the cybersecurity space. The U.N. Security Council first addressed the potential risks of AI during a 2023 meeting.

Anthropic (ANTHRO) CEO Dario Amodei introduced a strategy on September 12 that called for embedded evaluators, democratic coordination and global coordination to address the risks. It was announced today that Anthropic will indeed be embedding evaluators through a new partnership with Accenture (ACN).
